definitions.explanation: a standard-sized umbrella with a full-length handle, as opposed to a folding umbrella

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{長傘|なががさ}を{持|も}ってきた。
examples.english: I brought a long umbrella today.

examples.japanese: {長傘|なががさ}は{丈夫|じょうぶ}だけど、{持|も}ち{歩|ある}きに{不便|ふべん}だ。
examples.english: A long umbrella is sturdy, but inconvenient to carry around.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}に{長傘|なががさ}を{忘|わす}れてしまったので、{駅|えき}の{忘|わす}れ{物|もの}センターに{問|と}い{合|あ}わせた。
examples.english: I left my long umbrella on the train, so I contacted the station's lost-and-found center.

notes:
Composed of {長|なが} (long) + {傘|かさ} (umbrella, voiced to がさ by rendaku). Refers to the traditional full-length umbrella in contrast to a {折|お}りたたみ{傘|がさ} (folding umbrella). In everyday conversation, people often just say {傘|かさ} when they mean a long umbrella, since it was the standard type before folding umbrellas became widespread.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長傘|なががさ}を{差|さ}す: to open/use a long umbrella
- {長傘|なががさ}を{持|も}つ: to carry a long umbrella
- {長傘|なががさ}{立|た}て: umbrella stand (for long umbrellas)
- ビニール{傘|がさ}: vinyl umbrella (often long type)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {折|お}りたたみ{傘|がさ}: folding umbrella — compact and portable, the main alternative
- {日傘|ひがさ}: parasol — used for sun protection rather than rain
- {相合傘|あいあいがさ}: sharing an umbrella (with someone) — a romantic image in Japanese culture
